newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat futures end mixed amid USDA estimates.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat futures end mixed amid USDA estimates.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed despite perceptions that a USDA forecast for 1997 U.S. winter wheat production was bearish, traders said.
Analysts at a CBOT press briefing Friday said the CBOT soft red winter wheat futures contracts may have fallen to their seasonal harvest lows in anticipation of a large U.S. winter wheat crop.

"I think the bear has had his day and will have to be quite careful on pressing these levels," said John Zanutto, vice president for Merrill Lynch Futures. CBOT September wheat dropped early to a session low of $3.23 per bushel, just above the contract low of $3.21 that was set Tuesday.
USDA on Friday in its July wheat production forecast, pegged 1997 U.S. winter wheat production at 1.781 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 1.687 billion bushels.
But USDA also pegged total wheat production at 2.431 billion bushels, below the average analyst expectation for 2.433 billion.
CBOT wheat closed 1/4 cent a bushel lower to 3-3/4 up with July up 1/2 at $3.22. September was unchanged at $3.29-1/2.
